ai-at-work.excerpt: Nous Research, the open-source artificial intelligence startup backed by crypto venture firm Paradigm, released a new competitive programming model on Monday that it says matches or exceeds several la
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Nous Research dropped NousCoder-14B, an open-source coding model trained in four days on 48 Nvidia chips that claims to match larger proprietary systems. This matters because it shows open-source AI coding tools are getting genuinely competitive with Claude and others, which means your organization has real alternatives to vendor lock-in. That said, four days of training on enterprise-grade hardware isn't exactly something you can replicate in your own basement, so "open-source" still requires meaningful resources to actually use.

digital-culture.title: Why AI is burning women out
digital-culture.excerpt: Women spend twice as many hours per week as men on childcare and household work combined, and it starts before the alarm stops buzzing. A typical morning for me looks like waking the kids, discovering
digital-culture.dwp_take: A new report shows women are shouldering disproportionate domestic labor loads while also being expected to adopt AI tools that promise efficiency but often just pile on more tasks. This matters because digital workplace leaders keep selling collaboration tools and automation as universal solutions without acknowledging that "saving time" doesn't help when you're already drowning in invisible work. Here's the truth: giving someone who manages a household, three kids, and a full-time job an AI assistant is like giving a drowning person a faster swimming stroke.

digital-culture.title: Working through menopause symptoms? Try these tips
digital-culture.excerpt: More than half of women say they’re “not prepared at all” for perimenopause or menopause—yet most are already feeling the effects at work. According to recent data from InHerSight, a careers platform
digital-culture.dwp_take: Fast Company ran a piece highlighting that most working women feel unprepared for menopause despite three quarters experiencing symptoms that regularly impact their job performance. This matters because digital workplace leaders need to understand that a huge chunk of their workforce is dealing with a biological reality that nobody trained them for, yet they're still expected to show up and perform. The irony is thick: we've got wellness apps for everything, but somehow "your brain is foggy because your hormones are doing backflips" still doesn't make it into most company health conversations.
